thread:
Nina Gupta: quick sync: exploring claim-pruning for runtime tokens. goal: keep gateway path super tiny (< 1KB) while still supporting private/offline enforcement requirements. thoughts?
Owen Li: +1. two axes: what we put in token vs what we keep in policy store. runtime needs fast allow/deny for routes. prefer token -> reference id, gateway cache -> policy blob.
Ben Wu: agree. encoding full role graph bloats tokens. alternatives: numeric role ids + membership-ttl, or capability bitset per route. bitset is compact but brittle for rollout.
Sofia Morales: for Private installs, customers want zero external calls. we should support a policy bundle that gateways ingest and validate locally. bundle version in token so gateways know which policy snapshot to use.
Nina Gupta: good. so token minimal claims: issuer, subject, bundle_version, role_ids[] or membership_stamp. example:
```
{
  "iss":"redwood",
  "sub":"svc:ingest:42",
  "bv":"2026-03-20T12:00Z",
  "m":"r:12,r:34",
  "exp":1760003600
}
```
where m is membership shorthand. keeps token ~200-400 bytes.
Owen Li: plus we can do numeric compression: m: "12,34" and gateway maps to role defs. Also support a fallback header to trigger remote policy eval on miss.
Ben Wu: audit concern: if gateways only use local bundle we still need central audit of decisions. emit decision logs to central collector asynchronously. for Private installs, allow customer opt-in to ship logs back to us or keep local-only.
Sofia Morales: encryption/signing: bundles must be signed by our control plane; gateways verify signature with pinned public key. rotation plan: publish new key, support dual-signature during rollover window.
Nina Gupta: migration: many hosted API keys are long-lived. we can't force rotation. proposal: legacy keys mint a short-lived membership token on first use (adapter flow) and we record mapping. TTL short (5-15m). this reduces long-term exposure while letting customers keep old key.
Owen Li: perf: need microbenchmarks for bundle lookup and signature verify. gateway hot path should verify token signature (cheap RSA/ECDSA) + bundle cache hit. signature verify per-token might be heavy; consider session cache for verified tokens.
Ben Wu: another nuance: per-route parameterized permissions (e.g., allow ingest to dataset X). can't enumerate every dataset in role graph. solution: token contains scoped-id (dataset hash) + role reference. Gateway does match(dataset_hash, role perms) locally.
Sofia Morales: policy-as-code tooling: produce role -> route mappings and precompute per-bundle derived ACL tables for gateways to apply quickly. include TTL and diff stream for incremental updates.
policy-bot: added checklist item "bundle-signing-rotation-test" to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/policy-bundles
Nina Gupta: action items: 1) Owen: perf & cache sim (signature + bundle hit/miss) ; 2) Ben: audit logging model for local decisions & privacy opt-in; 3) Sofia: bundle format + delta feed spec; 4) I'll draft migration adapter sketch for legacy keys. target: RFC update next Tue.
Owen Li: I'll throw some numbers into the perf doc by Friday. aiming for <5ms overhead on gateway happy path.
Ben Wu: will outline audit schema and opt-in controls.
Sofia Morales: will prototype bundle JSON + signing example.
Nina Gupta: thanks, everyone. goal is small runtime tokens + robust offline policy support. keep tradeoffs in RFC (security, perf, migration, telemetry).
